requirements.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as a systemd service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: Unit file /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, enabled and started via systemctl. systemctl status and systemctl show confirm ActiveState=active, SubState=running, enabled, with MainPID pointing to the worker process. Verified both immediately after creation and again after a full node restart (new MainPID 734, still active/enabled).

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: id inventorysvc confirmed no prior existence; sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin inventorysvc created a dedicated system account. Unit file sets User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc. ps and systemctl show confirm both the shell wrapper and sleep child process run as inventorysvc/inventorysvc, not root. Re-confirmed after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/account state)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (513c865e...) and healthy service state captured before restart; 'sudo shutdown -r now' issued and acknowledged; boot_id polling showed connection failures during reboot then a new boot_id (786a8030...); post-reboot checks confirm inventory-worker.service active/enabled with a new MainPID still running as inventorysvc. Fixed global boot-identity snapshots (after_prepare=513c865e..., after_executor=786a8030...) independently corroborate the transition.

overall_summary: The executor created the inventorysvc system account, installed and enabled the inventory-worker.service unit wrapping /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, and verified via ps/systemctl that the running process is owned by inventorysvc rather than root — satisfying the task contract. It also completed the separate mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on node1: a healthy pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a directly observed boot-identity change, and confirmed post-reboot recovery of both the service and its dedicated-account ownership, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary mutations, failed services, or package-health issues were introduced.
limitations: Evidence is a bounded command trace; no independent access to the live node was available to re-verify current state beyond what was captured.
The worker script itself is a trivial sleep-loop stub, so its role validation is limited to process ownership/service state rather than functional business logic.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task requirements: useradd for the dedicated account (cmd-316cde1cd3ce41e1), unit file creation plus daemon-reload (cmd-3ff4bd5fa47b4bde), enable --now (cmd-51f3a19010e648b7), and the reboot cycle required by the restart evidence protocol (cmd-4bb42a9242144705). No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found; no failed services or package-health regressions appear in before/after snapshots. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small, expected byproduct of backgrounding the shutdown command for a clean acknowledgement — low-risk and not indicative of poor hygiene. The listening-sockets diff (sshd PID change) and rotated /tmp/systemd-private-* directories are normal artifacts of the reboot itself, not executor-introduced problems.
